Name: productive_vs_unproductive_token_signature
Title: Signal in the Noise: Mechanistic Signatures Separating Productive from Unproductive Reasoning Tokens
Short Hypothesis: Productive reasoning tokens (those that causally advance toward the correct answer) have a distinct activation signature-higher downstream causal influence and information gain-versus unproductive detours and hedges. This signature is decodable online and enables real-time reasoning-quality monitoring and pruning.
Related Work: Lightman et al. (2023) process reward models label step correctness with external supervision; Lanham et al. (2023) faithfulness. We derive an unsupervised, internal mechanistic signature of token productivity (causal influence + information gain) rather than a trained external verifier, tying it to efficiency.
Abstract: Not all reasoning tokens are equal: some advance the solution while others are detours or filler. We hypothesize a mechanistic signature-combining a token's causal influence on the final logits and its information gain about the answer-that distinguishes productive from unproductive tokens without external step labels. We estimate causal influence via activation patching (does replacing this token's contribution change the answer?) and information gain via the increase in a probe's answer-decodability across the token. We validate the signature against process-reward-model labels and human annotations of step usefulness. We then test online decodability: can a probe on local activations predict productivity before the trace completes? We apply it to (i) prune unproductive spans for efficient inference and (ii) as an intrinsic reward proxy for training shorter reasoning. We compare pruning quality and downstream efficiency to attribution and perplexity baselines, and to using a PRM directly. This bridges process-level interpretability with efficient reasoning by exposing, from internal signals alone, which parts of the model's thinking actually matter.
Experiments: 1. Build stepwise traces with PRM (e.g., Math-Shepherd) and small human-labeled subset as ground truth for productivity. 2. Compute per-token causal influence (patch token contribution to mean/pad) and probe-based information gain. 3. Correlate signature with PRM/human labels (AUC). 4. Train online productivity probe from local activations; evaluate lookahead-free prediction. 5. Prune low-productivity spans; measure accuracy vs compression, compare to attribution/perplexity and to PRM-guided pruning. 6. Optional: use signature as intrinsic reward in best-of-n reranking; measure token efficiency at fixed accuracy.
Risk Factors and Limitations: PRM labels are themselves imperfect ground truth. Causal-influence estimation is expensive and off-manifold. Productivity may be non-local (a token useful only in combination). Online prediction may be too weak. Intrinsic reward could be gamed, encouraging superficially 'productive-looking' tokens.
